insets.title: The gateway, the bench and the lamp

notes: Both hours use Scene 2's farm frame, +x east and +y north in metres from the lamp niche in the north gatepost, with the house door 34 m west on the gateway's axis.
At night Eliab tends the lamp from the road face of the niche, outside his own gate, so Amos comes out across the dark yard to the threshold to speak, and goes back in.
The night wind comes off the hills from the west, down the valley, so the flame leans out of the niche toward the road and holds.
Amos crosses the 34 m in real time, and the camera goes in to meet him and walks backward before him into the lamp's light, a baton pass from father to son and back.
The whip from Amos to his father lands on the answer in place at the post; the other joins inside each hour are continues and one stitch on the papyrus.
The gate and the house door stand open in every frame that reaches them, and Amos goes back in through the open lit door.
The first-light hour opens on the night's last frame, the same lens at the same spot, so one cut carries the hours at the gate.

From the house door the bench sits behind the north post and the 1.7 m wall, so Amos sees the lamp, the gateway and Micah and hears his father, and the lens on the road outside the gateway holds father and son in one deep frame.
Micah walks the south side of the lane so the far doorway stays clear in the deep frames, and stops before the bench with the wax.
The wax passes from Micah's hand to Eliab's, up to the last flame and down to the papyrus in one move, ending on the ring lifting and his hand shaking once.
